rustc 1.98.1 (48a229cea 2026-09-01)
binary: rustc
commit-hash: 48a229ceaefd4985c50990b14116b6d856af0985
commit-date: 2026-09-01
host: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
release: 1.98.1
LLVM version: 22.1.8

method.alternation: Rust,PARI on odd one-based pairs; PARI,Rust on even pairs
method.correctness: Every sample is checked for its exact arm-specific boundaryLabel and against the frozen discriminant, class number, and normalized invariant factors before its time is retained.
method.freshComputation: Every sample launches a fresh process and reconstructs from public coefficients; neither executable has a result cache.
method.nativeThreading: Rust cyclic and C2 x C(h/2) map construction for h>=10000 uses up to eight OS workers, capped by available parallelism. Native reduced-form enumeration and scalar class-number counting use up to eight workers when the candidate range has at least 20000 entries. Large eligible cyclic and odd three-prime-factor rank-two groups may use proved full-order prime-form orbits collected with up to eight native workers in place of separate enumeration and map traversal. Smaller Rust cases and Wasm use one worker. PARI has no matched worker pool, so ratios compare wall time, not equal CPU work.
method.timing: Reported kernel clocks exclude process startup and JSON projection. Rust includes coefficient validation, maximal-order preparation, enumeration, group construction, certificate construction, and internal verification. PARI includes nfinit0 plus bnfinit0 flag zero.

boundary.comparison: Both arms start from the same public monic polynomial. Rust returns a complete imaginary class-group certificate and exact ideal-class map; PARI flag zero also computes rank-zero unit/regulator data. Projection and process startup are excluded.

selection.coverageIntent: A diverse unconditional full-group comparison, including a genuine PARI 5--100 ms member if the independent campaign medians establish that band; no band is inferred from discriminant size.
selection.mathematicalOracle: The independently built PARI 2.17.4 public-call result projection supplied h and invariant factors; its internal clock was discarded during selection and not viewed or used for exclusion.
selection.primeEnumeration: Increasing exact primes, starting at each inclusive lower bound; draw counts include only primes satisfying the stated residue condition.
selection.rule: Retain the six structurally selected v1 fields but exclude its historically timing-nominated D=-9013587 candidate. For three new odd-prime fields, take the first prime p at or above 20e9, 40e9, and 60e9, respectively, with p mod 4 = 3, and set D=-p. For an even field, take the first prime p at or above 5e9 with p mod 4 = 1 and h(-4p) <= 50000, and set D=-4p. For a genus-rank-two composite field, take the first prime p at or above 1e9 with p mod 4 = 1 and h(-15p) <= 50000, and set D=-15p. The class-number cap is the predeclared Rust resource boundary; no PARI or Rust clock participates in selecting the new fields.

tinyBatchThroughput.selection: The original structural tiny panel is retained without timing-based exclusions.

promotion.step1: Integration owner commits/freezes engine, benchmark adapter, runner, panel, manifests, and lockfiles without this pre-promotion receipt.
promotion.step2: From a clean checkout of that frozen commit, rerun benchmark/run.py; require promotionEligible=true, matching clean source-closure status, reproducible binary hashes, and all exact checks before separately committing the generated receipt.

tinyBatchThroughput.method: Each sample is one fresh process; inside it every coefficient-only computation independently reconstructs and verifies the complete result without a result cache.
